title: What Is a Constitution?
text: A constitution is a foundational legal document that establishes the structure, powers, and limits of a government, and often enumerates the fundamental rights of citizens. Constitutions can be written (a single codified document, as in the United States or India) or uncodified, relying on a collection of statutes, conventions, and legal precedents (as in the United Kingdom). They typically serve as the supreme law of the land, superseding ordinary legislation.
